`efibootmgr`: show and change the EEPROM's boot entries and boot order.

## Synopsis

<strong>efibootmgr</strong> \[<strong>-v</strong>\] \[<strong>-q</strong>\] \[<strong>-c</strong>\
<strong>-d</strong> <em>disk</em> \[<strong>-l</strong> <em>path</em>\] \[<strong>-L</strong> <em>label</em>\]\] \[<strong>-b</strong> <em>XXXX</em> \[<strong>-B</strong>\]\] \[<strong>-o</strong> <em>X,Y</em> \| <strong>-O</strong>\] \[<strong>-n</strong> <em>X</em> \| <strong>-N</strong>\]

## Description

The EEPROM keeps boot variables in its NVRAM, as a UEFI board does: boot entries (<strong>Boot0000</strong> to <strong>Boot0007</strong>), each a disk by its id and a file on it; <strong>BootOrder</strong>, the order the entries are tried in; and <strong>BootNext</strong>, an entry tried once, at the next boot only. At power-on the EEPROM's bootloader tries <strong>BootNext</strong> (and clears it), then each entry of <strong>BootOrder</strong> whose disk is on the bus, then every disk in bus order holding <strong>/init.lua</strong>.

With no options, <strong>efibootmgr</strong> shows the variables. After a change it shows them as they are now, unless <strong>-q</strong>. Entry numbers are hexadecimal, as in <strong>Boot0001</strong>.

## Options

<strong>-c</strong>, <strong>--create</strong>
: Makes a new entry, numbered <strong>-b</strong>'s or the first free one, and puts it first in <strong>BootOrder</strong>.

<strong>-d</strong>, <strong>--disk</strong> \\fIdisk\\fR
: The new entry's disk: its name in <strong>/dev</strong> (<strong>storage1</strong>, <strong>/dev/storage1</strong>), or its id (<strong>id:\\fIuuid\\fR</strong>), which may name a disk that isn't on the bus yet.

<strong>-l</strong>, <strong>--loader</strong> \\fIpath\\fR
: The file the new entry boots; <strong>/init.lua</strong> when not given.

<strong>-L</strong>, <strong>--label</strong> \\fIlabel\\fR
: The new entry's label.

<strong>-b</strong>, <strong>--bootnum</strong> \\fIXXXX\\fR
: The entry <strong>-c</strong> makes or <strong>-B</strong> deletes.

<strong>-B</strong>, <strong>--delete-bootnum</strong>
: Deletes entry <strong>-b</strong>'s, from <strong>BootOrder</strong> and <strong>BootNext</strong> too.

<strong>-o</strong>, <strong>--bootorder</strong> \\fIX,Y\\fR
: Sets <strong>BootOrder</strong>.

<strong>-O</strong>, <strong>--delete-bootorder</strong>
: Clears <strong>BootOrder</strong>.

<strong>-n</strong>, <strong>--bootnext</strong> \\fIX\\fR
: Boots entry <em>X</em> next time only.

<strong>-N</strong>, <strong>--delete-bootnext</strong>
: Clears <strong>BootNext</strong>.

<strong>-v</strong>, <strong>--verbose</strong>
: Shows each entry's disk and file, and <strong>(not present)</strong> for a disk that isn't on the bus.

<strong>-q</strong>, <strong>--quiet</strong>
: Shows nothing after a change.

## Exit status

0 when done; 1 when the EEPROM refuses a change (why is on standard error: an id that isn't one, a path that isn't absolute, an entry that doesn't exist), or there's no EEPROM; 2 for bad usage.

## Files

<strong>/dev/eeprom</strong>
: The EEPROM, whose ioctls change the variables.

<strong>/sys/firmware/efi/efivars</strong>
: The variables, a file each, to read.

## Examples

```text
efibootmgr -v
efibootmgr -c -d storage1 -L "tiny OS"
efibootmgr -n 1
efibootmgr -o 1,0
efibootmgr -b 1 -B
```

## Notes

Linux's efibootmgr writes UEFI's variables, which name a partition by its GUID and a file on it; mcos's name a disk by its id. There is no <strong>BootCurrent</strong> and no active flag (<strong>-a</strong>, <strong>-A</strong>): every entry is active. The EEPROM checks every change, so a variable is always one its bootloader can read.

## See also

<strong>label</strong>(1), <strong>lsdev</strong>(1)
